statement: Produce a demographics table from an analysis results dataset (ARD): one column per treatment arm plus a Total column, each header showing the arm's N.
Produce an adverse events table by system organ class (SOC) and preferred term (PT), sorted by frequency, paged so that a SOC is not split from its first PT.
Keep only the preferred terms reaching an incidence threshold (for example 5% in any arm), keeping their SOC rows.
Produce a subject listing whose long text wraps within its column, paged by a row budget, with the column header on every page.
Embed a figure (a plot or an image file) on a page with its titles and footnotes.
Print a running page header and footer on every page, with the page number as 'Page x of y'.
Print the titles above and the footnotes below the table on every page.
Align the numbers of a column at the decimal point.
Split a table into one page (and section) per value of a by-group variable, each page named with its value.
Format the statistics with the number of decimals the study's standard gives (for example mean one more than the data, SD two more).
When no subject has an event, print one row saying so instead of an empty table.
Show a test's p-value from the ARD as a column beside the arms.
Split a table too wide for the page into blocks of columns, repeating the row labels on every block.
The same program on the same data writes the same RTF file every time.
Keep non-ASCII text (for example Japanese titles, labels and category values) unchanged in the RTF file.
Produce a subject disposition table: the number and percentage of subjects who completed the study or discontinued, by reason, one column per arm plus Total.
Produce an overview of adverse events: subjects with any TEAE, any serious, any related, any leading to discontinuation and any fatal TEAE, n (%) by arm.
Produce adverse events by SOC, PT and maximum severity: the severities (mild, moderate, severe) as columns under each arm.
Produce a laboratory summary by parameter and visit: n, mean (SD), median and range of the value and of the change from baseline under each arm.
Produce a laboratory shift table: the baseline category (low, normal, high) across under each arm, the post-baseline category down, n (%).
Produce a vital signs table by parameter and visit, with a blank row between the parameters.
Produce a PK concentration listing by subject and time point with its summary statistics under it in one table, a page per analyte and treatment.
Put a Kaplan-Meier plot, drawn by the study's own plotting code, on a page with its titles and footnotes.
Put a forest plot (estimates and confidence intervals by subgroup), drawn with ggplot2, on a page with its titles and footnotes.

Apply the company-standard look to every output from one style: font and size, title and footnote format and alignment, header and footer font and rules, table rules; a program's own setting still wins.
Set the paper size, orientation and the four page margins the company standard gives.
Assemble the outputs of a folder into one document with a table of contents in table-number order, each entry linked to its page, the pages numbered through the document.
Embed a figure given as a PNG file or as an EMF file (vector) at its size or the size given.
Print the program that wrote the output and the time it was written in the footer of every page.
